purpose: Tests the deterministic code-side normalization/comparison layer that runs between EXTRACT and VERIFY (D018 §2.3: 'arithmetic happens in code, never in the LLM'). Each case gives a claim-side and source-side numeric statement; the normalizer must decide (a) are they comparable at all, and only if so (b) are they equal. VERIFY never sees raw numbers — only this layer's comparable/equal output plus a note.
pass_bar: Zero false 'not comparable = contradicted'. Whenever comparable=false, the case must never be treated downstream as evidence of contradiction — a currency mismatch or missing unit is a data gap, not proof the claim is wrong. A false 'contradicted' from an incomparable pair is the one failure mode that accuses a customer's AI of an error it didn't make, and fails this golden set outright regardless of aggregate score.

expected.note: identical after normalization

correct computation from the same inputs yields ~16.6%/17%, not 25% — claimed derivation is arithmetically wrong

cases.trap_type: period mismatch — layer-boundary case, corrected after review

expected.note: the normalizer only sees structured (value, unit, scale, period-label) tuples — both sides are labeled 'Q2 2026 (three months)', same currency, same scale, so the normalizer correctly reports comparable=true, equal=false (254,940 ≠ 111,184 for the same stated period-label). It has no lookup to know 254,940 actually belongs to the six-month period — that requires the real source passage, which only VERIFY sees. So this case's job is narrower than the case name suggests: it proves the normalizer must NOT be the layer that decides 'unsupported' vs 'contradicted' here. That period-mismatch judgment belongs to VERIFY against the full passage (D018 §2.3, see verify-006), using this normalizer output only as one input, not as the final verdict.
